speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please describe the exact circumstances surrounding your episode of loss of consciousness, including how long it lasted and if you recall anything before or after. Did anyone witness the event to describe any jerking movements or bluish discoloration?

speaker: Patient
text: 53-year-old male. The patient was brought to the emergency department after an episode of loss of consciousness that occurred 1 hour ago, immediately after micturating. His wife found him unconscious on the bathroom floor. He regained consciousness after about 30 seconds without any confusion or amnesia for the event. No history of urinary incontinence during the event.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Commotio Cordis / Vasovagal Syncope secondary to bladder decompression (Micturition Syncope). Given the specific timing (immediately after urination) and the rapid recovery without confusion, this is highly suggestive of micturition syncope, a variant of vasovagal syncope, though commotio cordis is a differential if a physical impact occurred. I will proceed with ruling out cardiac arrhythmias. REQUEST TEST: ECG (Electrocardiogram). REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram.
